issues.main_description_html:
Description

  • Banner berubah setiap akses halaman dashboard.
  • API : https://github.com/GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New/blob/main/docs/v2/ads/get-banner-ads.md

Placement

The banner ad occupies the Banner image slot in the dashboard right rail, directly above the Upgrade to Pro card (see dashboard Workspace layout).

API contract (from the linked doc)

GET /v1/banner-ads/{app} — Auth: public

The endpoint picks one random banner from the eligible list per request, which is what produces a different banner on each dashboard visit.

Response (200):

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "messages": "Data retrieved",
    "code": "ADS.BANNER_SELECTED",
    "app": "gonav",
    "image_url": "https://example.com/banners/insta360x5.jpg",
    "direct_url": "https://www.insta360.com/..."
  }
}

Errors:

domainCode HTTP Condition
ADS.APP_NOT_FOUND 404 app key not present in the supported app map
ADS.NO_ADS_AVAILABLE 404 All ads are excluded for the given app

Acceptance Criteria

  • Fetch the banner from GET /v1/banner-ads/{app} when the dashboard page is accessed.
  • Render image_url in the dashboard right-rail banner slot (above Upgrade to Pro).
  • Clicking the banner opens direct_url (open in a new tab, with rel="noopener noreferrer").
  • A new banner is requested on every dashboard access, so the banner changes between visits (no caching that defeats rotation).
  • Show a loading/skeleton state in the banner slot while the request is in flight.
  • Handle ADS.APP_NOT_FOUND / ADS.NO_ADS_AVAILABLE (404) and network errors gracefully — hide the banner slot or fall back to the placeholder instead of breaking the dashboard layout.
  • Banner renders correctly in both light and dark mode, and is responsive across breakpoints.

Source

Branch product-docs
Created from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-editor-shapes-tools-brainstorming.md.

Goal

Add shape creation tools to the 2D editor toolbar so users can mark physical indoor objects such as tables, chairs, counters, fixtures, equipment, shelves, and other occupied spaces inside rooms.

Shapes are not rooms and are not decorative stickers. They represent non-walkable indoor objects in the Digital Twin, and direction lines should route around them instead of passing through them.

Scope

  • Add a Shapes dropdown to the 2D toolbar near Area, Point, and Safety tools.
  • Include Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon tools in the dropdown.
  • Support shape creation directly in the 2D panel.
  • Support Esc cancellation while drawing.
  • Support Shift precision behavior for rectangle and polygon creation.
  • Support selecting, moving, resizing, reshaping, deleting, undoing, and redoing completed shapes.
  • Treat completed shapes as non-walkable route obstacles.
  • Add a clear visibility option: Show shapes.

Recommended Toolbar Placement

Recommended 2D toolbar order:

  1. Wall
  2. Curve
  3. Window
  4. Area
  5. Shapes
  6. Point
  7. Safety
  8. Undo
  9. Redo

Tool Behavior

Rectangle

  • User selects Rectangle from Shapes.
  • User clicks first corner.
  • User clicks opposite corner.
  • Holding Shift creates a 1:1 square.
  • Esc cancels the unfinished rectangle.
  • After creation, user can adjust length, width, and position.
  • Rectangle blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Circle

  • User selects Circle from Shapes.
  • User clicks center or starting point.
  • User clicks radius point.
  • Circle starts as a 1:1 round shape.
  • Esc cancels the unfinished circle.
  • After creation, user can resize width and height, allowing the circle to become an oval.
  • Circle or oval blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Polygon

  • User selects Polygon from Shapes.
  • User clicks to place multiple points.
  • Polygon completes when the start and end points meet.
  • Holding Shift enables Snap to Grid for point placement.
  • Esc cancels the unfinished polygon.
  • After creation, user can move points, rearrange the object shape, and move the whole polygon.
  • Polygon blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Acceptance Criteria

Shapes Menu

  • Shapes appears as a grouped dropdown in the 2D toolbar.
  • Shapes contains Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  • The active shape type is understandable after selection.
  • Shape tools are treated as 2D editor tools, not 3D viewer controls.

Rectangle

  • User can create a rectangle by selecting two points.
  • Holding Shift creates a 1:1 square.
  • Pressing Esc during creation cancels the rectangle.
  • User can adjust rectangle length and width after creation.
  • Rectangle blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Circle

  • User can create a circle by selecting two points.
  • Circle starts as a 1:1 round shape.
  • Pressing Esc during creation cancels the circle.
  • User can adjust width and height after creation.
  • Circle can become an oval after editing.
  • Circle or oval blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Polygon

  • User can create a polygon with multiple points.
  • Polygon is completed when the start and end points meet.
  • Holding Shift allows point placement to Snap to Grid.
  • Pressing Esc during creation cancels the polygon.
  • User can rearrange polygon points after creation.
  • Polygon blocks direction lines from passing through it.

Editing and Visibility

  • User can select existing shapes.
  • Selected shapes show clear handles.
  • User can delete a selected shape.
  • Completed shape creation and edits can be undone and redone.
  • Shapes can be shown or hidden through a clear visibility option.

Style

  • Shapes follow the existing editor visual style.
  • Shape controls use compact icon-led toolbar patterns.
  • Shape fills and outlines do not overpower walls, rooms, points, safety annotations, or routes.

QA Scenarios

  • User opens Shapes and sees Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  • User creates a rectangle with two clicks.
  • User holds Shift while creating a rectangle and gets a square.
  • User presses Esc while drawing a rectangle and no rectangle is created.
  • User selects a rectangle and adjusts its length and width.
  • User creates a circle with two clicks.
  • User presses Esc while drawing a circle and no circle is created.
  • User selects a circle and resizes it into an oval.
  • User creates a polygon with multiple points.
  • User closes a polygon by returning to the starting point.
  • User holds Shift while placing polygon points and the points Snap to Grid.
  • User presses Esc while drawing a polygon and no polygon is created.
  • User selects a polygon and moves its points.
  • User creates a route near a rectangle and the route goes around it.
  • User creates a route near a circle or oval and the route goes around it.
  • User creates a route near a polygon and the route goes around it.
  • User places shapes so all paths are blocked and sees a no-route message.
  • User hides shapes and can show them again.
  • User uses Undo after creating a shape and the shape is removed.
  • User uses Redo after undoing a shape and the shape returns.
  • Keyboard-only user can open Shapes, select a shape tool, cancel with Esc, and delete a selected shape.

Suggested UI Copy

  • Shapes
  • Rectangle
  • Circle
  • Polygon
  • Click first corner.
  • Click opposite corner.
  • Hold Shift for square.
  • Click center.
  • Click radius.
  • Click to add points.
  • Click the first point to close.
  • Hold Shift to snap points.
  • Press Esc to cancel.
  • Shape selected
  • Delete shape
  • Object type
  • Object name
  • Routes avoid shapes.
  • No route available around this object.
  • Move or resize the shape to open a path.
  • Show shapes

Open Questions

  • Should shapes link to existing Information records, or should v1 keep only object name and type?
  • Should hidden shapes still block routes? Recommended default: yes, visibility controls display only.
  • Should route avoidance apply in editor preview only or all direction surfaces? Recommended default: all direction surfaces.
  • Should polygon editing support adding and removing points after creation? Recommended default: yes after basic point movement.

RESULT

Editor Shapes Tools implemented via subagent-driven-development (9 tasks + final review + polish). Rectangle/Circle/Polygon shape tools in the 2D editor:

  • Data model: Shape union + Model.shapes + shapeBoundary() (single geometry source); serialize/parse + level<->model bridge + undo history all carry shapes.
  • Toolbar Shapes dropdown (Rect/Circle/Polygon).
  • Drawing: rect 2-click (+Shift square), circle center->radius, polygon multi-point (+Shift snap, close-at-start), Esc cancel, live dashed preview.
  • Editing: select, move, resize (rect corners), reshape (circle rx/ry->oval, polygon vertices), delete; undo/redo; one-selection-at-a-time.
  • Render: subtle fill+outline+handles, layered below annotations; Show shapes toggle.
  • GeoJSON: each shape -> Polygon feature tagged {kind:shape, obstacle:true} (for future routing).

Route-obstacle avoidance (shapes block direction lines) DEFERRED to a follow-up per the approved spec.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-editor-shapes-tools-design.md
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-06-editor-shapes-tools.md
Commits: 9d65b79..d075369 on feature/186-editor-shapes-tools. Final review (opus): READY TO MERGE. tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 146 passed/3 skipped.

RESULT

Editor Shapes Tools shipped, plus two follow-ups, all merged to development.

#186 core — rect/circle/polygon shape tools in the 2D editor: draw, select, move, resize/reshape, delete, Show shapes toggle, persistence, GeoJSON obstacle export.

Follow-up 1 — Shapes 3D + map rendering: shapes render as extruded furniture in the three.js pane and on the maplibre map. Shape gains editable height + color; height slider + color picker; scene3d.ts extrusion pass; geojson-utils.ts shape features (active level) + fp-shape-extrusion/fp-shape-fill layers.

Follow-up 2 — Shape multi-select + group move/resize: selShape -> selShapes[]; Shift+click / marquee multi-select; 1 selected -> per-shape handles, 2+ -> group bbox + corner handles; group move + per-axis resize (Shift = uniform, clamped against invert/collapse); height/color/delete apply to all; toolbar "N selected". New pure shape-transform.ts with unit tests.

Verification: tsc --noEmit clean; touched files eslint-clean; full vitest 160 passed / 3 skipped. Final whole-branch review found + fixed a polygon group-scale mirror bug.

Merged via PR #198 (follow-ups -> #186 branch) and PR #199 (#186 -> development). development HEAD b87565d.

issues.display_title: Issue #197: Refresh editor Map mode tools and Information sidebar
issues.main_description_html:
Source

  • Brainstorming file: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-07-editor-map-mode-tools-brainstorming.md
  • Branch/source docs: product-docs

Goal

Refresh editor Map mode tools so the toolbar manages map/building controls and the sidebar manages level selection, object counts, and Information linking.

Toolbar Requirements

  • Add Select mode.
  • Add Drag building mode.
  • Make Select and Drag building a switch pair, where only one can be active at a time.
  • Add an Edit building dropdown with:
    • Rotate building
    • Scale building
    • Move up/down/left/right by button
    • Reset edits
  • Add a Show object dropdown with:
    • Show area label
    • Show point
    • Show shapes
    • Show safety annotation
  • Add a Map layer dropdown with:
    • Satellite
    • Vector
    • 3D building
  • Remove the old Floor dropdown grouping from the Map mode toolbar.
  • Remove the separate Show 3D Building tool from the Map tool area.

Sidebar Requirements

  • Add Select Level section.
  • Add Counter Object section with:
    • Total Objects
    • Total Linked
  • Add Information Linking Instructions:
    • Select an area, point, shape, door, or safety annotation, then connect it to an existing or new Information link.
  • Add Counter Total Information.
  • Add search by Information title.
  • Add Information list rows with:
    • Information title
    • Total linked count
    • Edit Info action
    • Delete Info action
    • Expand/collapse linked objects
  • Add linked object rows with:
    • Object icon
    • Object title
    • Unlink action
  • Hovering a linked object row highlights that object in the viewer.
  • Clicking a linked object row focuses or selects that object in the viewer.

Viewer Requirements

  • Remove Change Level from the map viewer.
  • Remove Level Labels from the map viewer.
  • Improve map tilt and rotation controls so they feel more interactive and user-friendly, similar to MappedIn.
  • Show object labels for:
    • Doors
    • Areas
    • Points
    • Safety annotations
    • Rectangles
    • Circles
    • Polygons
  • Object labels must show:
    • Object name
    • Linked or unlinked status
    • Information name when linked

Acceptance Criteria

  • Select and Drag building work as a clear switch pair.
  • The toolbar includes Select, Drag building, Edit building, Show object, and Map layer.
  • The old Floor dropdown is removed from Map mode.
  • Edit building groups rotate, scale, move, and reset.
  • Show object groups area labels, points, shapes, and safety annotations.
  • Map layer groups satellite, vector, and 3D building.
  • Separate Show 3D Building tool is removed.
  • Change Level and Level Labels are removed from the map viewer.
  • Level selection is handled in the sidebar.
  • The sidebar shows object counts and linked counts.
  • The sidebar gives clear Information linking instructions.
  • Information records can expand and collapse linked object lists.
  • Linked object rows can highlight and select objects in the viewer.
  • Doors, areas, points, safety annotations, rectangles, circles, and polygons have labels.
  • Labels show object name, linked/unlinked status, and Information name when linked.
  • Tilt and rotate controls feel more interactive and easier to understand.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign Editor mode drawing tools.
  • Do not redesign the whole editor page.
  • Do not remove the top Save, Preview, or Share actions.
  • Do not change project persistence behavior.
  • Do not add new Information content fields.
  • Do not add GoThru dashboard account connection behavior in this task.

RESULT

Branch: feature/197-map-tools-information-sidebar (from development)

Most toolbar/viewer-label requirements were already shipped by earlier tasks (#200, #207, #208): Select/Drag building switch pair, Edit building dropdown, Show object dropdown, Map layer dropdown (Street/Satellite/3D Building), old Floor dropdown + separate Show 3D Building tool removed, object labels for all kinds with linked/unlinked status and Information name, MapTiltControl. This task closed the remaining gaps:

Sidebar (Map mode) — EditorPanel.tsx, panel/InformationListSection.tsx

  • Select Level section (same block as Editor mode: level combobox + Add Level + Edit levels).
  • Counter Object section: Total Objects / Total Linked — counted via computeMarkerAnchors, the same enumeration the map marker overlay uses, so sidebar numbers always match the viewer.
  • Information linking instructions (spec copy).
  • Counter Total Information on the list header.
  • Information rows: expand/collapse chevron, title, linked count, Edit Info (opens InformationModal) and Delete Info (confirm dialog) actions.
  • Linked object rows: per-kind icon (area/door/point/safety/rect/circle/polygon), object title, Unlink action; hover highlights the object in the viewer, click selects it.
  • List now shows all Information records (not only ones linked on the active floor) so unlinked records can still be edited/deleted; linked counts stay per active floor.
  • Removed the redundant "Show labels" checkbox (toolbar Show object > Show area label covers it).

Store — useMapStore.ts / useMapStore.types.ts

  • New unlinkObjectInfo(kind, id) action clearing the Information link for every object kind on the active level (doors addressed by door-<index>).
  • deleteInformation now also clears infoId from shapes and floorplan doors (was leaving dangling ids).

Viewer — Editor3DMapView.tsx

  • Removed the FloorSelector overlay (Change Level) — level selection lives in the sidebar. PreviewOverlay keeps its own selector (preview is out of scope).
  • Removed the top-left floor-name badge (Level Labels requirement).

Verification

  • tsc --noEmit, eslint, pnpm build green.
  • vitest: 197 passed, 3 skipped — includes new useMapStore-unlink.test.ts covering unlinkObjectInfo for all kinds and deleteInformation clearing shapes/doors.

issues.display_title: Issue #226: Add Pano data layer: read tour overlay JSON into unified panorama list
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Data layer for the Add Panorama tool (#225): read a GoThru/TourMkr virtual tour link and turn it into a list of panoramas (names, positions, viewing angles, thumbnail, 360 image) ready to place on the map.

Full spec (non-technical narrative + verbatim field-path appendix):
docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-14-add-pano-data-fetching-brainstorming.md

The reading pipeline (6 steps)

  • Trim the key from the link — path segment starting with F1/G1, excluding the prefix (existing extractTourKey)
  • Resolve the tour: GET /v1/internal/tours/{tourKey} → id_user, cid, tour_id
  • Fetch overlay: https://gothru.co/moderation/{id_user}/{cid}/overlay/{tour_id}/overlay.json
  • Detect map type and read panoramas into one unified record (five recipes)
  • Per pano: open {pano_id}.json for thumbnail + 360 image (and children)
  • Hand to the Add Panorama tool (#225), routed by whether the pano has a map position

Five map types → unified record

Unified record: panoId, name, mapType, x, y, lat, lng, theta, phi, fov, radius, thumbnailUrl, imageUrl, children[]

Map type Position Placement (per #225)
Floor Map x/y Import & Apply Location (alignment overlay)
Journey Map x/y (+ children, recursive) Import & Apply Location
Mapbox lat/lng Import & Apply Location (pre-placed)
Splash Map none (angles only) Import → center cluster
No Map Plugin none (angles only) Import → center cluster

Exact widgets.map.dots[...] / widgets.other... field paths are in §10 of the spec (verbatim).

Implementation notes / dependencies

  • All gothru.co reads happen server-side (browser is CSP-blocked, like the existing panoramas proxy)
  • Add gothru.co (or image host) as an allowed image source, or proxy thumbnails
  • Floor/Journey background floor-plan image for the #225 alignment overlay is read from the overlay's map-widget config; fall back to #225 "missing asset map" behavior if absent
  • Error states: invalid link, tour not found, overlay unreadable, no map widget, empty list, missing pano image, mixed map types

Non-goals

  • No Add Panorama UI changes (that's #225)
  • No non-GoThru/TourMkr providers
  • No editing/re-hosting of 360 images
  • No caching strategy decision here

Source spec: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-14-add-pano-data-fetching-brainstorming.md · Companion to #225 · branch product-docs

RESULT

Data layer implemented on branch feature/226-add-pano-data-layer, commit 66c1111.

Files (+402 lines):

  • src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts — pure parser: detects the five map types and reads panoramas into the unified TourPanoRecord (field paths per spec §10; Splash/No-Map options found by key, never by index). attachImages() merges thumbnail/360 URLs recursively through Journey children.
  • src/actions/tours.ts — server action fetchTourPanoListAction(linkOrKey): extract key → GET /v1/internal/tours/{key} (Internal-API-Key from env) → fetch overlay.json → parse → merge images. Error codes per §8: input_invalid / tour_not_found / overlay_unreachable / no_map_widget; empty widget → empty list; missing image → empty URLs (placeholder).
  • src/lib/tourmkr/__tests__/overlay.test.ts — 9 tests covering all five map types, Journey recursion, null names, missing pano ids, image merge.

Verification: 212 tests pass, tsc clean, eslint clean. Parser validated against the live overlay of tour gvbw5zEr (No Map Plugin, 66 panoramas). Internal lookup + overlay URL pattern verified live end-to-end.

Deliberate deviations / notes:

  1. Step 5 (per-pano {pano_id}.json fetch) replaced with one call to the existing public panoramas API (fetchTourPanoramas) — it already returns thumbnail + 360 image for every panorama. N+1 fetches → 1 paginated call. Children still read recursively from overlay dots (Journey).
  2. The live internal API returns user_id (spec says id_user) — both accepted.
  3. Journey detection = any dot carrying children (parsing identical to Floor otherwise; misdetection only affects the label).
  4. Floor/Journey background image read best-effort from map-widget keys image/img/background/floorplan; null → #225 "missing asset map" fallback. No Floor Map sample tour was available to verify — flagged with ponytail: comments in code.
  5. "Allowed image source" dependency already satisfied: img.gothru.org is in the CSP img-src allowlist (next.config.ts) — zero change needed.

Commit: 66c1111

issues.display_title: Issue #227: Handle Issue Missing View Pricing Button in Footer in Dark Mode
issues.main_description_html:
Description

The View Pricing button in the footer is missing (not visible) when the app is in dark mode. In light mode the button renders correctly, but in dark mode it disappears — likely due to a color/contrast token making it blend into the dark footer background, or a conditional style hiding it.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Reproduce the issue: footer View Pricing button is not visible in dark mode.
  • Identify the root cause (color token, contrast, or conditional rendering/visibility).
  • The View Pricing button is visible and legible in dark mode with sufficient contrast.
  • The button remains correct in light mode (no regression).
  • Button styling stays consistent with the footer/design system in both themes.
  • Verified across the breakpoints where the footer renders.

issues.display_title: Issue #230: Surface upload errors in StepUploadFloor
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

In the setup wizard's upload step (src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx), a failed upload is invisible: xhr.onerror and non-2xx responses only set the progress bar to 100%, so the file looks successfully uploaded while its serverPath stays empty. The wizard then silently refuses to advance (allUploadsReady gate) with no explanation.

Why

Users see 100% progress and a stuck wizard with no error message — a silent failure and a support ticket generator.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Network error (xhr.onerror) pushes a clear message to the step's errors list
  • Non-2xx response (4xx/5xx) does the same, using the server's error message when present
  • The failed file row is visually marked as failed (not shown as complete)
  • User can retry or remove the failed file
  • Successful uploads behave exactly as before

Dependencies

None

RESULT

Branch feature/230-surface-upload-errors, commit 577f1b1 (+29/-8, 2 files).

  • StepUploadFloor.tsx — uploadToServer now fails loudly: network error, non-2xx response (server's error message used when present), and unparseable 2xx body all push a message to the step's error banner and mark the row failed via a progress -1 sentinel. Failed file keeps an empty serverPath, so the Continue gate stays closed — now with a visible reason.
  • FileListItem.tsx — failed rows get a destructive border + "Upload failed — remove and try again" hint; remove button (already present) is the retry path.

Verification: 212 tests pass, tsc + eslint clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #233: Stop forwarding gs_session cookie to project-file upload
issues.main_description_html:

Description

src/app/api/upload/route.ts forwards the gs_session cookie to the BE's POST /v1/projects/:id/file, but that endpoint stores files under the project UUID and never reads the session (the BE route comments say so explicitly). Remove the dead Cookie header; audit /api/files/route.ts for the same leftover on the project-file path.

  • Upload proxy no longer sends Cookie: gs_session=... to the project-file endpoint
  • /api/files project-file path checked and cleaned the same way (session-based legacy path untouched)
  • Upload and file GET flows work unchanged

None

RESULT

Branch feature/233-drop-gs-session-forward, commit f4dc3e9 (+10/-10, 4 files).

  • api/upload/route.ts — dropped Cookie: gs_session=... from the project-file POST forward.
  • api/files/route.ts — authHeaders() no longer forwards browser cookies on the project-file path (Bearer-only); the session-based legacy /v1/files path still forwards cookies as before.
  • Both route tests updated to assert the Cookie header is absent.

Verification: 212 tests pass, tsc clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #238: Wire Add Panorama UI (#225) to the tour pano data layer (#226)
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

Follow-up to #226 (data layer, merged) now that the #225 Add Panorama UI is ready: wire fetchTourPanoListAction into the tool so pasted tour links produce real rows and placement.

  • Modal 1 (Insert Tour Link): on Process, call fetchTourPanoListAction(link); render rows from TourPanoRecord[] (thumbnail thumbnailUrl, name — fallback label when empty, e.g. Mapbox has no names). Route each row's action by its own data: has x/y or lat/lng → Import & Apply Location, angles-only → Import (center cluster). "Import all" respects per-row routing.
  • Modal 2 (alignment): feed floorplanImageUrl as the tour asset-map overlay for floor/journey tours; null → #225 "missing asset map" fallback. Mapbox rows arrive pre-placed from lat/lng.
  • Error mapping (§8): input_invalid / tour_not_found / overlay_unreachable / no_map_widget / empty list → the #225 state messages; empty thumbnailUrl/imageUrl → placeholder, row still importable.
  • Verify the two flagged ponytail: assumptions in src/lib/tourmkr/overlay.ts against real tours during integration: Journey detection (children on dots) and the floor-plan image key (image/img/background/floorplan). Fix the parser if a real Floor/Journey tour disproves them.

Why

#226 built the data layer with no consumer; #225 built the UI on mock/placeholder data. This task connects them into the working feature.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Pasting a valid tour link lists its panoramas with thumbnails in Modal 1
  • Per-row Import / Import & Apply Location routing matches each record's position data

issues.display_title: Issue #236: Integrate address autocomplete + lat/lng-marker sync in Select Location
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Muhamad Rifky — Developer

Description

Wire the wizard's Select Location step (src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx) to the internal address-search service so address, coordinates, and the map marker stay in sync:

  1. Address autocomplete — typing in the address field queries the search API and shows suggestions; picking one auto-fills the latitude & longitude inputs and moves the map marker to that position.
  2. Lat/lng ↔ marker sync — editing the latitude/longitude inputs repositions the marker; moving the marker (or picking on the map) updates the inputs.
  3. Reverse geocode on marker drag — when the user drags the marker, the address field is updated by calling the place detail API with the new coordinates; a loading spinner shows in the address input while the request is in flight; concurrent drags are handled by dropping stale results.

Search API

  • GET http://{SEARCH_API_HOST}/search?q={query}&app_name=mapthru
  • Auth header: X-Search-Token — value from env (.env.local), never hardcoded or exposed to the browser; ask the team for the token value.
  • Host is LAN-internal (192.168.1.101:8081) and not in the CSP connect-src — calls must go through a server-side proxy (server action or route handler), same pattern as src/actions/panoramas.ts.

Place Detail API

  • GET http://{SEARCH_API_HOST}/places/coordinates?lat={lat}&lng={lng}
  • Same auth header (X-Search-Token) and proxy pattern as the search API.
  • Called server-side via getPlaceByCoordinatesAction in src/actions/search.ts.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Typing an address shows autocomplete suggestions from the search API (debounced; no request per keystroke)
  • Selecting a suggestion fills lat & lng inputs and moves the marker to the selected position
  • Manually editing lat/lng moves the marker; moving the marker updates lat/lng inputs
  • Dragging the marker reverse-geocodes the new position and fills the address field
  • Address input shows a loading spinner during reverse geocode; concurrent drags drop stale results
  • Search token read from env server-side only; no token in client bundle or repo
  • Empty results / API failure degrade gracefully (no crash, inputs stay manually usable)

Dependencies

None

RESULT

Implemented full address autocomplete + lat/lng-marker sync for the Select Location wizard step.

Files changed:

  • src/actions/search.ts — new server action; proxies GET /search (autocomplete) and GET /places/coordinates (reverse geocode) through Next.js server; token never exposed to client
  • src/components/setup/StepSelectLocation.tsx — debounced (350ms) autocomplete dropdown, suggestion pick syncs address+lat+lng to store, loading spinner during reverse geocode
  • src/components/map/MapLibreCore.tsx — fixed stale closure on moveend listener (was capturing initial onLocationChange, wiping address on every programmatic fly); added isUserMove flag via e.originalEvent
  • src/components/map/MapViewer.tsx — propagated isUserMove to callback type
  • src/components/setup/WizardShell.tsx — reverse geocode on user drag with stale-result guard (seq ref); loading state via addressLoading in store
  • src/store/useMapStore.ts + useMapStore.types.ts — added addressLoading state
  • .env.example — added SEARCH_API_HOST and SEARCH_TOKEN placeholders

Description
